title: Influence of a nurse-led nutritional assessment and individual nutritional adaptation on the clinical course of enterally fed neurological/neurosurgical early rehabilitation patients
summary:
Background
Many people with severe diseases of the brain or nervous system who are treated in early rehabilitation receive liquid nutrition through a feeding tube. These patients are at risk of not receiving enough energy and nutrients, which may negatively affect their recovery, increase complications, and prolong hospital stay. In everyday care, nutritional problems are not always identified early or managed in a structured way.
Research Question
This study aims to investigate whether a structured nutrition assessment led by specially trained nursing staff, combined with individualized adjustment of tube feeding, can improve recovery compared with usual care.
Methods
The study will compare two groups of patients treated at different time periods. One group will receive usual care. The second group will receive a structured nutrition assessment shortly after admission, regular review of nutritional needs, individualized adjustment of tube feeding, and ongoing monitoring during the hospital stay. Recovery, nutritional status, complications, and length of hospital stay will be compared between groups. In addition, nursing staff will be asked about their experiences with implementing the approach in daily practice.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥18 years
Primary neurological or neurosurgical diagnosis (ICD-10-GM: I60–I69, S06; optionally G00–G99 according to study protocol)
Requirement for enteral nutrition via feeding tube (e.g. PEG, PEJ, nasogastric or nasojejunal tube)
Expected hospital length of stay of at least 7 days
Written informed consent from the patient or legal representative
Exclusion criteria:
Age below 18 years
No requirement for enteral nutrition (adequate oral nutrition possible)
Expected hospital length of stay of less than 7 days
Palliative situation with primarily symptom-oriented treatment
Lack of informed consent from the patient or legal representative
Participation in another interventional study with potential influence on nutritional status or functional outcomes
